'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Insurgency in Cabo Delgado]]
**[[Battle of Palma]]
***[[Mozambique]]'s [[Mozambique Defence Armed Forces|military]] says that it has regained full control of the town of [[Palma, Mozambique|Palma]], more than a week after it was captured by [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|ISIL]]-linked [[militant]]s. Several militants are killed during the [[counter-offensive]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-56637573 (BBC News)]
*[[War in Darfur]]
**[[2021 Darfur clashes]]
***Tribal clashes between [[Masalit people|Masa]] and [[Sudanese Arabs|Arabs]] in the [[Sudan]]ese city of [[Geneina]], [[West Darfur]], kill at least 40 people and injure 60 others. Residents report the use of heavy weaponry and [[rocket-propelled grenade]]s. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/4/5/eighteen-dead-as-violence-escalates-in-sudans-west-darfur-region (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Insurgency in Southeastern Nigeria]], [[prison breaks in Nigeria]]
**[[Owerri prison break]]
***Authorities say that heavily-armed gunmen attacked a prison in [[Owerri]], [[Imo State|Imo]], [[prison escape|freeing more than]] 1,800 prisoners. Police accuse the banned [[separatist]] group [[Indigenous People of Biafra]] of being the attackers. The group denies the allegations, calling them "lies". [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-africa-56644577 (BBC News)]
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]
**The Afghan Army Special Operations Division reportedly says that 110 [[Taliban]] members have been killed in the last 24 hours in [[Afghanistan]]. [https://en.mehrnews.com/news/171735/110-Taliban-members-killed-in-Afghanistan (Mehr News Agency)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[South Korea]]n [[electronics]] company [[LG Electronics|LG]] says that it will discontinue producing [[smartphone]]s, citing poor sales and stiff competition from both flagship and budget brands. It becomes the first major smartphone brand to exit the market. [https://www.bworldonline.com/lg-becomes-first-major-smartphone-brand-to-withdraw-from-market/ (''BusinessWorld'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*At least 26 people are killed when a ferry sinks after [[Ship collision|colliding]] with a [[cargo ship]] in the [[Shitalakshya River]], [[Narayanganj]], [[Bangladesh]]. [https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/world/south-asia/bangladesh-ferry-disaster-death-toll-rises-to-20-official/articleshow/81910465.cms (''The Times of India'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
****[[India]] reports a record 103,558 new confirmed cases of [[COVID-19]] in the past 24 hours, thereby making it the second country after the [[United States]] to report more than 100,000 new cases in a single day. [https://m.timesofindia.com/india/indias-daily-covid-19-cases-surpass-100000-mark-for-first-time/amp_articleshow/81906729.cms (''The Times of India'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Iran]]
****[[Iran]] receives over 700,000 doses of the [[Oxford-AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford-Astrazeneca]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] manufactured by [[SK Group|SK Bioscience]] and supplied through the [[COVAX]] initiative. [https://www.tehrantimes.com/news/459485/First-batch-of-COVAX-vaccine-arrives-in-Tehran (''Tehran Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines]]
****The [[Philippines]] surpasses 800,000 cases of COVID-19. [https://news.abs-cbn.com/news/04/05/21/philippines-covid19-cases-800000-april52021 (ABS-CBN News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Saudi Arabia]], [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on Hajj]]
****The [[Ministry of Hajj and Umrah (Saudi Arabia)|Ministry of Hajj and Umrah]] says that only vaccinated pilgrims will be allowed access to [[Mecca]]'s [[Masjid al-Haram|Great Mosque]] during [[Ramadan]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/4/5/saudi-to-permit-only-vaccinated-pilgrims-from-ramadan-on (Al Jazeera)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
***Restrictions in [[Byron Bay, New South Wales]], and surrounding areas are lifted following a decline in cases. This was the last area of Australia to be under any form of lockdown. [https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2021/apr/05/northern-nsw-snap-covid-restrictions-to-be-lifted-at-midnight (''The Guardian'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*The [[Government of Turkey|Turkish government]] arrests at least ten former [[Admiral of the fleet (Turkey)|admirals]] under suspicion of initiating a [[coup d'état]], after 104 retired admirals issued an open letter opposing the proposed [[Istanbul Canal]]. [https://www.thenews.com.pk/latest/815257-at-least-10-former-admirals-arrested-in-turkey-over-open-letter-on-montreux-convention (''The News International'')]
*The [[United States Customs and Border Protection]] agency announces the separate arrests of two [[Yemen]]i nationals on the [[Federal Bureau of Investigation|FBI]]'s terrorism watchlist attempting to enter the country from [[Mexico]] earlier this year. [https://www.thetimes.co.uk/article/two-yemeni-men-arrested-at-us-border-identified-on-fbi-terror-list-rkpv6lhh8 (''The Times'')]
*A relative of [[Red Crescent]] worker Abdulrahman al-Sadhan says the [[Saudi Arabia]]n Specialised Criminal Court has sentenced al-Sadhan to 20 years imprisonment, followed by a 20-year travel ban, in a [[secret trial]]. Rights groups allege the sentence is connected to an anonymous [[Twitter]] account on which al-Sadhan questioned Saudi positions on [[human rights]] issues. [https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/saudi-terror-court-aid-worker-Abdulrahman-Sadhan-20-years-prison (Middle East Eye)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Politics of Vietnam]]
**[[Nguyễn Xuân Phúc]] is elected as the [[List of presidents of Vietnam|11th]] [[President of Vietnam|President]], with 97.5% of the vote. He is the [[Vietnam|country]]'s [[List of Prime Ministers of Vietnam|first former]] [[Prime Minister of Vietnam|Prime Minister]] to be elected President. [https://vnexpress.net/ong-nguyen-xuan-phuc-lam-chu-tich-nuoc-4257880.html (VnExpress)]
**The [[National Assembly of Vietnam]] elects [[Phạm Minh Chính]] as the [[Vietnam|country]]'s [[List of prime ministers of Vietnam|10th]] [[Prime Minister of Vietnam|Prime Minister]], with 96% of the vote. [https://zingnews.vn/tan-thu-tuong-pham-minh-chinh-post1200885.html (Zing)]
*[[2020 amendments to the Constitution of Russia]]
**[[President of Russia|President]] [[Vladimir Putin]] signs a law extending the [[President of Russia|presidential]] [[term of office]] to a total of four consecutive six-year terms. The law would allow Putin, who is on his second consecutive term, to serve as president until 2036. [https://news.abs-cbn.com/overseas/04/06/21/putin-signs-law-allowing-him-to-serve-2-more-terms (ABS-CBN News)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2021 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament]]
**The [[2020–21 Baylor Bears basketball team|Baylor Bears]] defeat the [[2020–21 Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball team|Gonzaga Bulldogs]], [[2021 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Championship Game|86-70]], handing [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]] their first loss of the season and winning the [[NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament|NCAA men's basketball tournament]]. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/baylor-wins-ncaa-tournament-beating-gonzaga/ (CBS News)]
